back_blocks.md: The **empirical formula** shows the **simplest whole-number ratio** of atoms in a molecule, while the **molecular formula** shows the **actual number** of atoms.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Carbon dioxide is classified as an organic compound.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
By convention, **carbon dioxide** (and carbon monoxide and metal carbonates) are **not** classified as **organic compounds**, even though they contain carbon.

front_blocks.md: What does a **displayed formula** show that a structural formula does not?

back_blocks.md: A **displayed formula** shows **every atom** and **every bond** in the molecule. A **structural formula** omits most covalent bonds and only shows key bonds such as double bonds.

cards.front_md: What does a **displayed formula** show that a structural formula does not?

front_blocks.md: Define **homologous series**.

back_blocks.md: A **homologous series** is a family of organic compounds that share the same **functional group**, the same **general formula**, similar **chemical properties** and a gradation in **physical properties**. Each member differs from the next by CH<sub>2</sub>.

front_blocks.md: Define **functional group**.

back_blocks.md: A **functional group** is a group of atoms bonded in a specific arrangement that determines the **chemical properties** of the homologous series it belongs to.

All members of a homologous series have the same general formula.

front_blocks.md: What is the general formula for the alkane homologous series?

back_blocks.md: The general formula for **alkanes** is C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n+2</sub>, where n is the number of carbon atoms in the chain.

front_blocks.md: Define **prefix** (organic naming).

back_blocks.md: A **prefix** (or stem) in an organic compound's name indicates the number of carbon atoms in the **longest continuous carbon chain**: meth- (1), eth- (2), prop- (3), but- (4), pent- (5) and hex- (6).

front_blocks.md: What is the IUPAC name for a straight-chain alkane with four carbon atoms?

back_blocks.md: The name is **butane**. The prefix **but-** indicates four carbon atoms and the suffix **-ane** shows it belongs to the **alkane** family (no functional group other than single C–C bonds).

The suffix **-anol** indicates that a compound belongs to the alcohol family and contains an –OH functional group.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Propene contains two carbon atoms.

back_blocks.md: **False.**

**Propene** contains **three** carbon atoms. The prefix **prop-** always means three carbons. The suffix **-ene** indicates that propene contains a **C=C double bond** and belongs to the alkene homologous series.

front_blocks.md: How do you name the **position isomers** of an unbranched alkene?

back_blocks.md: Position isomers of an unbranched alkene are named by placing a **number** before the suffix **-ene** to show the carbon where the double bond starts. For example, **but-1-ene** has the double bond starting on carbon 1, while **but-2-ene** has it starting on carbon 2.

front_blocks.md: Define **IUPAC nomenclature**.

back_blocks.md: **IUPAC nomenclature** is the internationally agreed system for naming organic compounds, using a **prefix** to show chain length and a **suffix** to show the functional group.

front_blocks.md: Define **addition reaction**.

back_blocks.md: An **addition reaction** is one in which two or more molecules combine to form a single larger molecule with **no other products**.

front_blocks.md: In a **substitution** reaction, one **..........** is replaced by another, whereas in an **addition** reaction, molecules combine to form a **..........** with no other products.

back_blocks.md: In a **substitution** reaction, one **atom** (or group of atoms) is replaced by another, whereas in an **addition** reaction, molecules combine to form a **single larger molecule** with no other products.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The reaction of ethene with bromine is classified as an addition reaction.

back_blocks.md: **True.**

Bromine adds **across the double bond** of **ethene** to form **dibromoethane** (C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub>Br<sub>2</sub>) with no other products, which is the defining feature of an **addition** reaction.

front_blocks.md: What are the three reaction types used to classify reactions of organic compounds at IGCSE?

back_blocks.md: The three types are **substitution**, **addition** and **combustion**.

front_blocks.md: Methane reacts with bromine under ultraviolet light. What type of reaction is this and what are the products?

back_blocks.md: This is a **substitution** reaction. One hydrogen atom is replaced by bromine, giving **bromomethane** (CH<sub>3</sub>Br) and **hydrogen bromide** (HBr) as products.

front_blocks.md: **Complete combustion** of a hydrocarbon requires **..........** oxygen and produces **..........** and water as the only products.

back_blocks.md: **Complete combustion** of a hydrocarbon requires **excess** oxygen and produces **carbon dioxide** and water as the only products.

cards.front_md: **Complete combustion** of a hydrocarbon requires **..........** oxygen and produces **..........** and water as the only products.
cards.back_md: **Complete combustion** of a hydrocarbon requires **excess** oxygen and produces **carbon dioxide** and water as the only products.

front_blocks.md: How does incomplete combustion of a hydrocarbon differ from complete combustion in terms of products?

back_blocks.md: **Incomplete combustion** occurs when oxygen supply is limited. Instead of **carbon dioxide**, the products include **carbon monoxide** (and possibly soot/unburned carbon). **Water** is produced in both cases.
